doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Personnel and feel of the Blakey band
summary: She lists musicians who came through Blakey's band and calls it a jungle of energy.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, that’s fantastic. Who was in the band at that point?
I’m trying to remember. Carlos Garnett was in there. I haven’t heard him in a long time but I see he had a record out, I think it was last year, a new CD out. Actually the tour we

did Etta Jones was on but she wasn’t singing there. The bass player changed. It was Skip Crumby-Bey, but it changed to Jan Arnet, someone from Czechoslovakia that we only saw then. Of course we did go through several bass players and different people. And I think it was Randy Brecker, but he didn’t do some of the tours with us. We had Bill Hardman and we also had Woody Shaw, and other tenor players came in later, Ramon Morris, I think Buddy Terry did one job with him. So it was kind of a moving group.
He had a lot of energy, that band, didn’t he?
Yeah, he did. It was just like a jungle, it was great.
